title: Define difficulty per skill
statement: Define each difficulty level per skill and check every label against that skill's own definition, because one global rule for easy or hard mislabels items.
example: Across 1,888 judged items, difficulty alignment caused 564 failures, second only to factual accuracy.
detail: Across 1,888 judged math items, difficulty alignment was the second most common failure, with 564 failures (40.0%) after factual accuracy's 650 (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md`, lines 11 and 52-56). The judge read each standard's own definitions, for example finding an item labelled easy that matched the medium definition for its standard (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/FAILURE_PATTERN_ANALYSIS.md`, line 23). A grade 4 curriculum file defines the levels per skill, for example by which step of a pattern the question asks about (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/edu_configs/curriculum_grade_4.jsonl`, line 1). A pass-rate analysis traced the failures to generic guidance such as "EASY: small numbers" (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/PASS_RATE_ANALYSIS.md`, line 81); that is its diagnosis, not a measurement.
against: The pipeline then hard-coded one number range per level for every skill, "'easy': (100, 999)," (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/FIX_SUMMARY.md`, line 71), and its README reports "<1% range errors (was 15%)" (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/README.md`, line 197) with no scored run cited for it.

evidence.quote: Comprehensive analysis of 1,888 existing test questions across grades 4, 6, 7, and 8 with a quality threshold of 0.85.
- **Issue:** Labeled as Easy but matches the provided Medium definition for this standard.
"difficulty_matrix": "EASY\n- Steps one to three are given and the question asks about step 4.
- Generic difficulty guidance ("EASY: small numbers") doesn't match specific requirements
